summary: # How to Make a Doll in Marvelous Designer? Happy New Year from the Rabbit Doll! ## Introduction Hello, everyone! In this tutorial video, we will learn how to make a rabbit doll using Marvelous Designer. ## Creating the Doll's Base First, we create a circular board with a diameter of 300 mm in the 2D window. Then, we press the **W** key to click on the top of the board in the 3D window. ### Adding Pins Next, add a pin to prevent the board from falling to the ground after the simulation is turned on later. ### Using the Dragon Layer Then, use the inner layer of the dragon layer to create a layer of the dragon layer. The dragon-shaped board will be automatically pasted near the original board. Here, we choose the inner dragon layer, so the created board will be pasted to the inner part of the original board. ### Texture Surface Clarification If you usually use a dense texture surface, you may not be able to distinguish the front from the back. After switching to the texture surface, you can see that the front of the board is white while the back is black. ## Flipping the Board Now, select the board on the back side, right-click, and turn it over. This ensures that these two boards are facing outward. ## Inflating the Boards Next, we need to inflate these two boards, which means adding pressure. We add pressure to 10 here and then press the control key to start the simulation. ### Adjusting Particle Diameter To achieve a better detail effect, we reduce the particle diameter of these two boards to 10 and start the simulation. After reducing the particle diameter, we notice some wrinkles along the powder line. ## Adjusting Fabric Properties To correct this, we go to **Fabric** to make some adjustments to the physical properties of the fabric in the fabric window. After selecting the fabric in the property editor, reduce the fineliner strength of the fabric and the tension of the foot line. The fineliner strength controls the stretching performance of the fabric; smaller numbers yield better stretching. ### Pressure and Density Adjustments Since the fabric now stretches easily, it will expand like a balloon under pressure with no wrinkles. The bottom of the board's stretching performance is too good, so we need to reduce its density a little. This adjustment makes it appear to float in 3D space. ### Modifying Simulation Properties Due to some problems with the fixed needle, we can right-click in the 3D background and select the simulation property. Then, go to the property editor and set the force to 0. With no force in the 3D environment, the whole board will float freely. ## Creating the Rabbit's Face Now that we have the ball body, we can start making other details, beginning with the rabbit's face. ### Drawing the Inner Line Here, we use the internal multidirectional line tool to draw an inner line along the middle line of the board. After selecting this inner line, we choose **Cut and Sew**. Now, the front piece is divided into left and right symmetrical halves since the rabbit's face is symmetrical. ### Adjusting the Forehead Next, we use the adjustment board tool to select these two boards, right-click, and select the symmetrical board and sewing line at the bottom of the movable board. This way, after we modify one board, the other will adjust simultaneously. #### Drawing the Forehead Line To create the forehead, draw an inner line diagonally and select **Cut and Sew**. While drawing lines, press the control key to create a curve point, and double-click to complete the creation. ### Merging the Forehead After cutting and sewing, we can select the middle line of the forehead board, right-click, and select **Merge**. This makes the forehead a single board, linking the left and right sides. ## Adjusting Facial Features Now, we need to adjust the rabbit's face. Since the nose and mouth are prominent structures, we can use the editor board tool to select the mouth line and extend it outward to widen the rabbit's face. ### Shaping the Chin Next, press **Control + C** to switch to the editor tool and drag the neckline down to create a meaty effect on the chin. ## Fixing Board Position Since the pressure is balanced, we have added some fabric that may cause pressure imbalance. Press the **W** key again and click at the chin to fix the board. ### Aligning the Rabbit's Head If the rabbit's head is crooked, select all boards with **Control + A**, rotate with the positioning tool, and freeze the head behind. ### Enhancing the Nose After increasing the rabbit's face board, if the nose position is still not prominent enough, we can extend the mouth line outward a little more. ## Finalizing the Rabbit's Head To ensure the mouth and nose have a prominent effect, we increase the fabric, which may require adjusting the forehead board to match its length on both sides with the face board. ### Adjusting Overlapping Boards After adjusting, move the board in the 2D window so they do not overlap. We can freeze the front forehead board to fix the rabbit's head in 3D space and untangle the back headboard to let it participate in the simulation. ### Pin Fixation The front line is used here to fix the pin; you can also select it and delete it if necessary. ## Making the Rabbit's Body Let's start making the rabbit's body. For more intuitive confirmation, we can use the 3D board tool to draw some reference lines on the 3D board. ### Sewing the Body Panels The sewing method is the same as sewing the inner line: click and hold the **Control** key to create a curve and double-click to complete the creation. To ensure the rabbit is symmetrical, we cut the back piece along the middle line. ### Applying Symmetry After sewing, we apply symmetry. Now that the symmetry is set, we can return to the 3D window and find the edit line 3D board tool to select the 3D line we just created. ## Converting to Inner Shape In the right-click menu, choose to convert to the inner shape. Because the panels are symmetrical, the inner line created will also be automatically created on the other side. ### Cleaning Up Extra Lines If there are extra inner lines, we can delete them and select the inner line that has not been extended to the outer line of the panel, extending it accordingly. ## Creating the Body Panel Next, we use the rectangular tool to draw a panel approximately the width of this inner line. Click and hold the **Control** key to change it to the inner line of the panel. ### Freezing the Top Panel To maintain the current simulation form, we freeze the top panel first. Click and hold the **Control** key to start the simulation. ## Creating Symmetrical Panels After the simulation is complete, go back to the 2D window, select this panel, and press **Control + D** to create a symmetrical panel. Then, merge the front and middle panels together. ### Rearranging Panels Select the front panel and copy it as the back panel. In the 3D window, rearrange it to fit the back panel. ## Sewing the Sides Continue to use the line powder tool to sew the lines, keeping in mind the direction of the line of powder. ### Simulating the Effect To simulate the effect, we need to select these new panels and modify their pressure since the bottom of the panel is now open, causing it to lack balance and float around. ### Closing the Bottom We need to use the line powder tool to sew the bottom together, paying attention to the direction of the line of powder. ## Shaping the Body Now, the body panel resembles a small pillow. We need to use the circular curve tool to draw an angle that matches the front and back panels. ### Modifying Panel Shapes If the body panel is too short and not round enough, we can modify the panel shape. First, stretch the point of the waist out to widen it. ### Using the Pen Tool After modifying the front panel, remember to modify the back panel simultaneously. Use the pen tool to cut some curves on the side for a rounder, smoother look. ## Adjusting the Body Length Next, adjust the length of the body since the width of the front and back panels is not the same. After applying pressure, the panel will fall back, so we can adjust it. ### Adding Pins Press **W** and click to add a pin and fix the current position. Then, we can choose to freeze the back panel. ## Making the Rabbit's Feet First, let's draw two internal circles for the feet, adjusting their size in the 3D window. Then, select the front panel and reduce its particle diameter to 10 for a smoother circle. ### Measuring and Sewing Measure the length of half of the ellipse and draw a rectangular panel to sew on top. The width of this rectangular panel needs to match half of the circle, while its height can be created based on your needs. ## Creating Foot Panels When sewing, select a whole section first, then press the **Shift** key to select the lines with only sewing, and finally loosen the **Shift** key to complete the creation. ### Adjusting Foot Panel Sizes Here, we copy and paste a new panel and create the rest of the sewing lines. Then we create a foot panel using the adjustment panel
